A_baseline.constraint_state: committed routed checkpoint, no new constraints

B_impossible_budgets.purpose: red-first: prove the analysis reacts to the constraints
B_impossible_budgets.constraints: i2s output delay +200 ns; spi_miso output delay +81.0 ns

C1_committed_i2s_min_minus_8_2.purpose: diagnose the phantom hold violations of -min -8.2
C1_committed_i2s_min_minus_8_2.finding: the check demands data arrive >= 8.2 ns AFTER the i2s_bclk port arrival (~9.667 ns): a minimum-skew demand at the coincident launch/capture pair. The RTL never switches SDATA/LRCLK on rising-edge cycles (rtl-sketch/i2s_tx.v:48), so the pair is a phantom and the demand is not the DAC's requirement.

C2_committed_candidate.constraints: i2s_bclk_ext generated clock /4; i2s -max 8.200, -min 154.560; spi_miso -max 54.958/-min 0; led[*] 0/0 (all as separate -max and -min commands)
C2_committed_candidate.no_output_delay_classification: 0 unconstrained (HIGH); 0 excused by false paths; 1 port with a timing clock defined on it (LOW): i2s_bclk

D_candidate_plus_bclk_output_delay.purpose: test putting a nominal output delay on the forwarded-clock port itself
D_candidate_plus_bclk_output_delay.finding: an output delay on i2s_bclk against its own generated clock fails a self-referential hold check (the data path IS the clock path). The generated clock stays the port's only constraint; Vivado classifies the port as 'no output delay but with a timing clock defined on it' (LOW).
